title: CBS Radio Workshop
paragraphs: CBS's mid-1950s experimental radio anthology, using drama, documentary techniques, sound, music, and literary adaptation to explore what storytelling could do in the radio medium.
CBS experimental anthology blending drama, documentary technique, literary adaptation, music and sound experimentation.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Friday experimental anthology (January 27, 1956 to October 26, 1956) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Sunday experimental anthology (November 4, 1956 to September 22, 1957) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include William N. Robson (director, producer, and radio adaptor), [[person|william-conrad|William Conrad]] (performer, narrator, and announcer), Hugh Douglas (announcer and performer), Ben Wright (performer and author), Luis Van Rooten (performer and narrator), Ralph Bell (performer and narrator), and [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], [[org|org.bc515a817083485c|WGBI]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.c02e02e51669c221|WCBS-FM]].

The stories often return to technology, media and modern systems, experimental radio and sound form, literary adaptation and authored texts, music and sound as narrative material, social satire and contemporary society, and science fiction and speculative futures.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Revival of the Columbia Workshop experimental tradition, Network radio experimentation during the television era, and Sound-first experimental production.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|suspense|Suspense]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
